question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

Work in two steps. First, in the candidates field, brainstorm 20 candidate ideas, one line each, covering as wide a range as you can. Then select the 5 candidates that best combine being non-obvious with being feasible and informative, and develop those as your ideas.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment reporter tracking linked to retrospective single-cell profiling
ideas.description: Use live-cell fluorescent reporters (e.g., CDK2 activity, cell-cycle or stress-pathway sensors) to follow individual cells through drug exposure and record their fate. Then profile the tracked cells retrospectively (e.g., by fixing and sequencing or by photo-labelled recovery) to identify which pre-treatment states predict survival.

ideas.title: Lineage barcoding to distinguish pre-existing from drug-induced tolerance
ideas.description: Label each founder cell with a unique heritable DNA barcode before treatment and track barcode frequencies through drug exposure and recovery. If survivors come from a small set of pre-marked clones, tolerance was pre-existing; if barcodes are randomly represented, tolerance is induced by the drug.

ideas.title: Per-cell intracellular drug quantification
ideas.description: Measure how much drug each cell actually accumulates, using fluorescent analogs of the drug or LC-MS on flow-sorted cells. Test whether survivors have lower intracellular drug levels due to uptake or efflux differences rather than altered target biology.

ideas.title: Chromatin accessibility priming and causal perturbation
ideas.description: Profile chromatin accessibility by scATAC-seq in drug-naive cells and identify regions that are open in cells that later survive. Then perturb the implicated chromatin regulators to test whether they causally change survival fraction.

ideas.title: Pooled CRISPR screen with single-cell transcriptomic readout
ideas.description: Run a genome-wide knockout screen under drug treatment with single-cell RNA readout so each perturbation's effect on both survival and cell state is measured together. This separates genes that drive survival from those that merely mark a tolerant state.

candidates: Single-cell RNA-seq of drug-naive population to find pre-existing transcriptional states that predict survival
DNA lineage barcoding to test whether survivors derive from pre-existing clones or drug-induced switching
Time-lapse imaging with fluorescent cell-cycle or kinase reporters, linking each cell's pre-treatment state to its fate
scATAC-seq of pre-treatment cells to identify chromatin priming that marks future persisters
Perturbation of chromatin regulators (e.g., KDM5A, EZH2) to test whether epigenetic state causally controls survival
Pooled CRISPR knockout screen comparing survivors with unsorted cells to find genes that enable survival
Perturb-seq with single-cell readout to link individual gene knockouts to changes in drug-tolerant state
Per-cell intracellular drug quantification by fluorescent drug analogs or sorted-cell LC-MS to test uptake and efflux heterogeneity
ABCB1 and other efflux-pump expression heterogeneity measured by flow and sorted for drug challenge
Mitochondrial membrane potential or OXPHOS heterogeneity sorted by TMRM and tested for drug survival
Single-cell metabolomics (Raman or mass spec imaging) to detect metabolic states of survivors
Cell-cycle or quiescence phase at time of drug exposure, measured with FUCCI reporters
Measuring stochastic gene expression noise and transcriptional bursting in single cells over time
Mass cytometry of phospho-signaling networks to identify signaling heterogeneity before and after drug
Spatial transcriptomics or imaging of organoids to test whether niche position or neighbor contact predicts survival
Paracrine or conditioned-media experiments to test whether neighboring cells secrete survival factors
Deep sequencing of survivors to detect pre-existing subclonal resistance mutations at low allele frequency
Extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) copy-number quantification per cell by imaging or single-cell DNA-seq
Drug-pulse and holiday timing experiments to probe the dynamics of entry into and exit from the tolerant state
Machine learning on pre-treatment morphology or time-lapse features to predict which cells survive
